expectations.text: Names all three review items: legal review of published terms, code of conduct and insurance; privacy review of attendee data moving into sales systems; and anti-bribery/gifting review of hosted guests.
expectations.evidence: Hospitality clearance, attendee data into Salesforce, and terms/conduct/insurance.

expectations.text: Sequences the privacy review before registration opens, because the notice has to be right at the moment the data is collected - making the 3-week date the binding one.
expectations.evidence: "Your privacy owner reviews it before the form is built, because the notice must be right at the moment of collection."

expectations.text: States that piping the registration feed into the sales systems is a personal-data decision, not a reporting or integration task, owned by whoever holds the company's privacy obligations.
expectations.evidence: "This is a personal-data decision, not a reporting one."

expectations.text: Lists what that privacy review covers: the lawful basis, the notice shown at registration, the retention rule, and the limits on internal reuse.
expectations.evidence: Lawful basis, the notice, the retention rule, and limits on internal reuse.

expectations.text: Names no jurisdiction, statute, or specific retention period, routing the actual rules to the company's own counsel.
expectations.evidence: "Your counsel decides the actual rules and jurisdictions. I name none here."

expectations.text: States the reversibility asymmetry for the data decision: a list collected under the wrong notice cannot be un-collected, and correction usually means not using what was collected.
expectations.evidence: "a list collected under the wrong notice can't be un-collected, and the fix usually means not using it."

expectations.text: Flags the hosted federal-agency and bank guests: the guest's employer's rules are frequently stricter than the host's and are not the host's to waive.
expectations.evidence: "each guest's employer's policy, which is often stricter and is not yours to waive."

expectations.text: Notes public-sector and regulated-industry guests are the common case where an ordinary hospitality item is not permitted at all.
expectations.evidence: "For public-sector and regulated-industry guests, an ordinary flight-plus-two-nights package may not be permitted at all."

expectations.text: Quotes no specific gift or hospitality monetary threshold.
expectations.evidence: Asks counsel about a "value cap" but names no figure.

expectations.text: Sequences the gifting review before invitations go out, stating that an invitation accepted under a rule it breached cannot be undone by either side.
expectations.evidence: "an invitation accepted under a rule it breaks is unrecoverable, and the cost lands on the guest as well as on you."

expectations.text: Notes the goal consequence: a goal that depends on hosting specific accounts depends on those accounts being permitted to accept, so this is asked before the goal is agreed.
expectations.evidence: The goal step (step 2) never links hosting specific accounts to the goal, and hospitality is not tied to the goal decision.

expectations.text: States the terms review includes how the code of conduct binds company staff as well as guests, with the enforcement path existing before an incident.
expectations.evidence: "a code of conduct that binds your own staff as well as guests, with an enforcement path for when the person reported is an employee"

expectations.text: States the terms reversibility: a published term can be revised for the next edition, but an incident at this one cannot be revised at all.
expectations.evidence: "Terms can be revised next year. An incident this year can't."
